claim: NKG2D is an immunoreceptor expressed on the surface of NK cells and some T cells.
source: NKG2D is an important immunoreceptor expressed on the surface of NK cells and some T cells.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and introduction, and is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: NKG2D recognizes a set of ligands typically expressed on infected or transformed cells.
source: NKG2D recognizes a set of ligands typically expressed on infected or transformed cells, but recent studies have also documented NKG2D ligands on subsets of host non-tumor cells in tumor-bearing animals and humans.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Recent studies have documented NKG2D ligands on subsets of host non-tumor cells in tumor-bearing animals and humans.
source: NKG2D recognizes a set of ligands typically expressed on infected or transformed cells, but recent studies have also documented NKG2D ligands on subsets of host non-tumor cells in tumor-bearing animals and humans.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Tumor-associated macrophages are induced to express the NKG2D ligand RAE-1δ in transplanted tumors and genetically engineered mouse cancer models.
source: Here we show that in transplanted tumors and genetically engineered mouse cancer models, tumor-associated macrophages are induced to express the NKG2D ligand RAE-1δ.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 1 and related text.

claim: A soluble factor produced by tumor cells is responsible for macrophage RAE-1δ induction.
source: We find that a soluble factor produced by tumor cells is responsible for macrophage RAE-1δ induction, and we identify tumor-derived colony-stimulating factor-1 (CSF-1) as necessary and sufficient for macrophage RAE-1δ induction in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 2 showing conditioned medium induces RAE-1δ.

claim: Tumor-derived CSF-1 is necessary and sufficient for macrophage RAE-1δ induction in vitro and in vivo.
source: We find that a soluble factor produced by tumor cells is responsible for macrophage RAE-1δ induction, and we identify tumor-derived colony-stimulating factor-1 (CSF-1) as necessary and sufficient for macrophage RAE-1δ induction in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 2-5 showing CSF-1 induces RAE-1δ and blocking CSF-1 prevents induction.

claim: Induction of RAE-1δ on macrophages by CSF-1 requires PI3K p110α kinase signaling.
source: Furthermore, we show that induction of RAE-1δ on macrophages by CSF-1 requires PI3K p110α kinase signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 6 showing PI3K p110α inhibitors block RAE-1δ induction.

claim: Production of CSF-1 by tumor cells leading to activation of PI3K p110α represents a novel cellular and molecular pathway mediating NKG2D ligand expression on tumor-associated macrophages.
source: Thus, production of CSF-1 by tumor cells leading to activation of PI3K p110α represents a novel cellular and molecular pathway mediating NKG2D ligand expression on tumor-associated macrophages.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion stated in the abstract and supported by the collective experimental data.

claim: In mice, NKG2D ligands include the RAE-1 family (including isoforms α, β, γ, δ, and ε), the H60 family (a, b, c), and MULT1.
source: In mice, these include the RAE-1 family (including isoforms α, β, γ, δ, and ε), the H60 family (a, b, c), and MULT1.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Human NKG2D ligands include the ULBP family (with isoforms 1–6) and the MICA and MICB proteins.
source: Human NKG2D ligands include the ULBP family (with isoforms 1–6) and the MICA and MICB proteins (Raulet et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Acute ligation of NKG2D on NK cells transmits a powerful activation signal through the DAP10 and DAP12 adaptors, triggering NK cell release of cytotoxic granules and pro-inflammatory cytokines such as interferon-γ.
source: Acute ligation of NKG2D on NK cells transmits a powerful activation signal through the DAP10 and DAP12 adaptors, triggering NK cell release of cytotoxic granules and pro-inflammatory cytokines such as interferon-γ (Raulet, 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Steady-state interactions of NKG2D with ligands in vivo cause NK cells to adopt a state of global desensitization to acute activation.
source: In contrast, recent studies have shown that steady-state interactions of NKG2D with ligands in vivo, such as with endogenous expression of RAE-1ε in mice (Thompson et al., 2017) or transgenically enforced overexpression of various NKG2D ligands in vivo (Oppenheim et al., 2005; Wiemann et al., 2005), cause NK cells to adopt a state of global desensitization to acute activation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: NKG2D has been implicated as a co-stimulatory molecule for T cells.
source: NKG2D has also been implicated as a co-stimulatory molecule for T cells (Bauer et al., 1999; Markiewicz et al., 2005), and in some cases NKG2D can mediate lymphocyte trafficking to sites of inflammation (Markiewicz et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: NKG2D can mediate lymphocyte trafficking to sites of inflammation.
source: NKG2D has also been implicated as a co-stimulatory molecule for T cells (Bauer et al., 1999; Markiewicz et al., 2005), and in some cases NKG2D can mediate lymphocyte trafficking to sites of inflammation (Markiewicz et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: Various auto-inflammatory conditions, such as atherosclerosis in a mouse model, have been shown to be mediated in part by NKG2D.
source: Various auto-inflammatory conditions, such as atherosclerosis in a mouse model, have also been shown to be mediated in part by NKG2D (Ogasawara et al., 2004; Xia et al., 2011; Guerra et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Most cells in healthy mice lack surface NKG2D ligand expression.
source: Most cells in healthy mice lack surface NKG2D ligand expression, whereas many tumors and infected cells show expression in vitro and in vivo (Raulet et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: Many tumors and infected cells show NKG2D ligand expression in vitro and in vivo.
source: Most cells in healthy mice lack surface NKG2D ligand expression, whereas many tumors and infected cells show expression in vitro and in vivo (Raulet et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: NKG2D ligand expression on diseased cells is usually understood as a cellular response to stresses associated with transformation or infection.
source: In general, NKG2D ligand expression on diseased cells is usually understood as a cellular response to stresses associated with transformation or infection (Eagle et al., 2006; Mistry and O'Callaghan, 2007; Raulet et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: NKG2D ligands are induced in mouse and human cells as a result of an activated DNA damage response.
source: A prominent example is the induction of NKG2D ligands in mouse and human cells as a result of an activated DNA damage response (Gasser et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: Rapidly proliferating fibroblasts upregulate NKG2D ligands in vitro and in vivo independently of the DNA damage response, due to transactivation of the promoter of the Raet1e gene by E2F transcription factors.
source: Subsequent studies found that rapidly proliferating fibroblasts upregulate NKG2D ligands in vitro and in vivo independently of the DNA damage response, due to transactivation of the promoter of the Raet1e gene (which encodes RAE-1ε) by E2F transcription factors (Jung et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: Heat shock stress and the integrated stress response have been implicated in NKG2D ligand expression.
source: Heat shock stress and the integrated stress response have also been implicated in NKG2D ligand expression (Groh et al., 1996; Venkataraman et al., 2007; Nice et al., 2009; Gowen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: In some cells, steady-state expression of micro-RNAs may confer post-transcriptional regulation of NKG2D ligand expression.
source: In some cells, steady-state expression of micro-RNAs may confer post-transcriptional regulation of NKG2D ligand expression (Heinemann et al., 2012; Codo et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: In human but not mouse cells, activation of p53 has been implicated in NKG2D ligand induction.
source: In human but not mouse cells, activation of p53 has also been implicated in NKG2D ligand induction (Li et al., 2011; Textor et al., 2011; Iannello et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Toll-like receptor (TLR) agonists induced NKG2D ligands on mouse macrophages and human monocyte-derived dendritic cells.
source: For example, Toll-like receptor (TLR) agonists induced NKG2D ligands on mouse macrophages and human monocyte-derived dendritic cells (Hamerman et al., 2004; Ebihara et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Tumor-associated myeloid cells and circulating monocytes in glioblastoma patients were shown to upregulate NKG2D ligands.
source: Tumor-associated myeloid cells and circulating monocytes in glioblastoma patients were shown to upregulate NKG2D ligands (Crane et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: In transplant and spontaneous mouse models, tumor-associated endothelial cells were found to induce high levels of the NKG2D ligand RAE-1ε.
source: In transplant and spontaneous mouse models, tumor-associated endothelial cells were found to induce high levels of the NKG2D ligand RAE-1ε (Thompson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: Expression of RAE-1 molecules was found on macrophages infiltrating a mouse model of melanoma and a model of lymphoma.
source: Expression of RAE-1 molecules was also found on macrophages infiltrating a mouse model of melanoma and a model of lymphoma (Deng et al., 2015; Nausch et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Tumor-associated macrophages in B16 tumors expressed RAE-1δ but not other NKG2D ligands.
source: Interestingly, TAMs in B16 tumors expressed RAE-1δ but not other NKG2D ligands (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1A.

claim: RAE-1δ was weakly expressed on monocytes in B16 tumors but negligible on other hematopoietic cells.
source: In addition to strong expression on TAMs, RAE-1δ was weakly expressed on monocytes in B16 tumors (identified as CD45-pos; CD11b-hi; Ly6G-neg; F4/80-low; Ly6C-hi – gating strategy in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A) – but negligible on other hematopoietic cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1B.

claim: RAE-1δ staining on TAMs was completely absent in RAE-1-KO mice, confirming the specificity of the RAE-1δ staining.
source: Importantly, RAE-1δ staining on TAMs was completely absent in RAE-1-KO mice, which contain frameshift mutations in the genes encoding RAE-1δ and RAE-1ε, confirming the specificity of the RAE-1δ staining (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Splenic macrophages, peritoneal macrophages, and blood monocytes in mice bearing B16 tumors expressed little to no RAE-1δ.
source: In contrast to robust TAM expression of RAE-1δ, splenic macrophages, peritoneal macrophages, and blood monocytes in mice bearing B16 tumors expressed little to no RAE-1δ (Figure 1—figure supplements 1C and 3B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1—figure supplements 1C and 3B,C.

claim: Macrophages within the B16 tumor microenvironment are induced to express the NKG2D ligand RAE-1δ.
source: These data indicate that macrophages within the B16 tumor microenvironment are induced to express the NKG2D ligand RAE-1δ.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the data presented in Figure 1.

claim: Expression of RAE-1δ in TAMs within B16 tumors was similar at various stages of tumor growth.
source: Expression of RAE-1δ in TAMs within B16 tumors was similar at various stages of tumor growth (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: RAE-1δ staining was negligible or very low on TAMs in RMA-S tumors.
source: In contrast to the findings with B16 tumors, RAE-1δ staining was negligible or very low on TAMs in similarly sized S.C. tumors generated by injection of the RMA-S T cell lymphoma cell line (5 × 106 cells injected) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1C.

claim: TAMs in primary KP sarcomas expressed robust RAE-1δ.
source: In the KP sarcoma model driven by lentiviral-Cre activation of oncogenic Kras and deletion of Trp53 (DuPage et al., 2009), TAMs in primary tumors expressed robust RAE-1δ (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1C.

claim: TAMs within primary TRAMP prostate tumors mostly lacked RAE-1δ.
source: In contrast, TAMs within primary TRAMP prostate tumors -- a spontaneous adenocarcinoma model driven by expression of SV40 T antigens (Greenberg et al., 1995) -- mostly lacked RAE-1δ (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1C.

claim: Tumor microenvironments are differentially capable of inducing NKG2D ligand expression by macrophages.
source: Thus, tumor microenvironments are differentially capable of inducing NKG2D ligand expression by macrophages.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the differential expression patterns observed across tumor models.

claim: Macrophages cultured in control medium showed little to no RAE-1δ expression.
source: Macrophages cultured in the control medium showed little to no RAE-1δ expression, but culture with B16-conditioned medium led to a robust induction of cell surface RAE-1δ (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2A.

claim: Culture with B16-conditioned medium led to a robust induction of cell surface RAE-1δ on macrophages.
source: Macrophages cultured in the control medium showed little to no RAE-1δ expression, but culture with B16-conditioned medium led to a robust induction of cell surface RAE-1δ (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2A.

claim: RAE-1δ was induced by culture medium from a KP sarcoma cell line.
source: RAE-1δ was similarly induced by culture medium from a KP sarcoma cell line (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2B.

claim: A soluble factor(s) produced by B16 tumor cells and KP sarcoma cells is sufficient to induce RAE-1δ on macrophages ex vivo.
source: These results indicated that a soluble factor(s) produced by B16 tumor cells and KP sarcoma cells is sufficient to induce RAE-1δ on macrophages ex vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the conditioned medium experiments.

claim: Recombinant CSF-1 was sufficient to induce robust RAE-1δ expression on macrophages.
source: Alone among the cytokines tested, recombinant colony-stimulating factor-1 (CSF-1), also known as macrophage colony-stimulating factor (MCSF), was sufficient to induce robust RAE-1δ expression on macrophages (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2C.

claim: Macrophages cultured with recombinant CSF-1 along with blocking antibody against CSF-1R failed to induce RAE-1δ.
source: Macrophages express the CSF-1 receptor (CSF-1R) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), and macrophages cultured with recombinant CSF-1 along with blocking antibody against CSF-1R failed to induce RAE-1δ, establishing that the added cytokine acts through CSF-1R (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2C.

claim: Recombinant CSF-1 caused upregulation of transcripts of the Raet1d gene, which encode RAE-1δ.
source: We performed qPCR on reverse-transcribed RNA from CSF-1-stimulated macrophages and found that recombinant CSF-1 caused upregulation of transcripts of the Raet1d gene, which encode RAE-RAE-1δ (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by qPCR data in Figure 2D.

claim: As little as 3 ng/ml CSF-1 was sufficient to induce detectable RAE-1δ, with high induction levels seen at 10 ng/ml.
source: Stimulation with graded doses of CSF-1 showed that as little as 3 ng/ml was sufficient to induce detectable RAE-1δ in this system, with high induction levels seen at 10 ng/ml (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Induction of other NKG2D ligands by CSF-1 was negligible.
source: Interestingly, induction of other NKG2D ligands by CSF-1 was negligible (Figure 2E), indicating that CSF-1 upregulates RAE-1δ highly selectively.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2E.

claim: CSF-1 upregulates RAE-1δ highly selectively.
source: Interestingly, induction of other NKG2D ligands by CSF-1 was negligible (Figure 2E), indicating that CSF-1 upregulates RAE-1δ highly selectively.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the data in Figure 2E.

claim: Macrophages derived from bone marrow cells via 7 days of culture with CSF-1 induced robust RAE-1δ.
source: Consistent with our findings, macrophages derived from bone marrow cells via 7 days of culture with CSF-1 induced robust RAE-1δ, whereas parallel cultures in GM-CSF showed little to no RAE-1δ expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Macrophages cultured in GM-CSF showed little to no RAE-1δ expression.
source: Consistent with our findings, macrophages derived from bone marrow cells via 7 days of culture with CSF-1 induced robust RAE-1δ, whereas parallel cultures in GM-CSF showed little to no RAE-1δ expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: B16 cells secreted substantial CSF-1.
source: As measured by ELISA of cell culture supernatants, B16 cells secreted substantial CSF-1, whereas RMA-S cells did not (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by ELISA data in Figure 3A.

claim: RMA-S cells did not secrete CSF-1.
source: As measured by ELISA of cell culture supernatants, B16 cells secreted substantial CSF-1, whereas RMA-S cells did not (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by ELISA data in Figure 3A.

claim: KP sarcoma cell lines produced CSF-1, and much more robustly than did B16 cells.
source: KP sarcoma cell lines also produced CSF-1, and much more robustly than did B16 cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by ELISA data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The concentrations of intratumoral CSF-1 were much greater in B16 tumors than in RMA-S tumors.
source: We used ELISA to analyze CSF-1 protein levels in tumor microenvironments in vivo from mechanically dissociated S.C. tumors and found the concentrations of intratumoral CSF-1 were much greater in B16 tumors than in RMA-S tumors (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by ELISA data in Figure 3B.

claim: The level of CSF-1 within B16 tumors was substantially greater than serum CSF-1 levels in naïve or tumor-bearing mice.
source: Furthermore, the level of CSF-1 within B16 tumors was substantially greater than serum CSF-1 levels in naïve or tumor-bearing mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), consistent with previous reports describing steady-state CSF-1 levels in circulation (Menke et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by ELISA data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: CSF-1R blockade completely abrogated macrophage RAE-1δ induction by B16-conditioned medium.
source: We found that CSF-1R blockade completely abrogated macrophage RAE-1δ induction by B16-conditioned medium (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3C.

claim: RAE-1δ induction by KP cell line-conditioned medium was completely prevented by antibody blockade of CSF-1R.
source: RAE-1δ induction by KP cell line-conditioned medium was also completely prevented by antibody blockade of CSF-1R (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3D.

claim: CSF-1 is sufficient to induce RAE-1δ on macrophages.
source: Collectively, these data indicated that CSF-1 is sufficient to induce RAE-1δ on macrophages, and that CSF-1 is necessary for macrophage RAE-1δ induction by B16 and KP tumor cell supernatants in vitro.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the data presented in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: CSF-1 is necessary for macrophage RAE-1δ induction by B16 and KP tumor cell supernatants in vitro.
source: Collectively, these data indicated that CSF-1 is sufficient to induce RAE-1δ on macrophages, and that CSF-1 is necessary for macrophage RAE-1δ induction by B16 and KP tumor cell supernatants in vitro.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the data presented in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Blockade of CSF-1 or CSF-1R led to substantial reductions in RAE-1δ expression by TAMs in B16 tumors.
source: Mice with established B16 tumors were treated with anti-CSF-1 or anti-CSF-1R, and RAE-1δ on TAMs was analyzed 48 hr post-treatment. Blockade of CSF-1 or CSF-1R each led to substantial reductions in RAE-1δ expression by TAMs (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4A.

claim: Blockade of CSF-1R for 2 days had no impact on macrophage cell numbers but drastically reduced macrophage RAE-1δ expression in B16 tumors.
source: Blockade of CSF-1R for 2 days had no impact on macrophage cell numbers but drastically reduced macrophage RAE-1δ expression, whereas treatments for 5 days or longer caused a major depletion in TAM numbers, associated with low RAE-1δ levels on the few remaining macrophages (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Treatments with CSF-1R antibody for 5 days or longer caused a major depletion in TAM numbers in B16 tumors.
source: Blockade of CSF-1R for 2 days had no impact on macrophage cell numbers but drastically reduced macrophage RAE-1δ expression, whereas treatments for 5 days or longer caused a major depletion in TAM numbers, associated with low RAE-1δ levels on the few remaining macrophages (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: A 2 day treatment with CSF-1R antibody resulted in a substantial reduction in RAE-1δ on TAMs in primary KP tumors without a significant reduction in TAM numbers.
source: Similar to the findings with B16 tumors, a 2 day treatment with CSF-1R antibody resulted in a substantial reduction in RAE-1δ on TAMs in primary KP tumors without a significant reduction in TAM numbers, generalizing our findings to spontaneous tumors (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Antibody blockade of the CSF-1/CSF-1R axis suppresses RAE-1δ expression by TAMs in B16 S.C. tumors and autochthonous KP sarcomas.
source: Thus, antibody blockade of the CSF-1/CSF-1R axis suppresses RAE-1δ expression by TAMs in B16 S.C. tumors and autochthonous KP sarcomas.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the data presented in Figure 4.

claim: Csf1-KO B16 tumors showed markedly lower RAE-1δ expression by TAMs compared with control tumors.
source: Compared with control tumors, Csf1-KO B16 tumors showed markedly lower RAE-1δ expression by TAMs (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 5A.

claim: A second, independent Csf1-KO B16 clone also showed substantially reduced RAE-1δ expression by TAMs.
source: Mice injected with a second, independent Csf1-KO B16 clone also showed substantially reduced RAE-1δ expression by TAMs (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 5B.

claim: Csf1-transduction completely reversed the KO phenotype, and restored RAE-1δ expression on TAMs.
source: To control for off-target effects of Cas9, Csf1-KO B16 cells were stably transduced with control empty vector or a Csf1-expression vector, and injected into mice. Csf1-transduction completely reversed the KO phenotype, and restored RAE-1δ expression on TAMs (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 5C.

claim: RMA-S cells stably transduced with a CSF-1-expression vector efficiently induced RAE-1δ expression by TAMs.
source: In contrast, RMA-S cells stably transduced with a CSF-1-expression vector efficiently induced RAE-1δ expression by TAMs whereas transduction with empty vector had little or no effect (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 5D.

claim: Production of CSF-1 by tumor cells in vivo drives RAE-1δ expression on tumor-associated macrophages.
source: Collectively, these data provide decisive evidence that production of CSF-1 by tumor cells in vivo drives RAE-1δ expression on tumor-associated macrophages.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the data presented in Figure 5.

claim: Macrophages showed robust S6 phosphorylation after CSF-1 stimulation.
source: First, we analyzed activation of the PI3K pathway by intracellular flow cytometry for phosphorylated-S6, a known downstream target of PI3K signaling, in peritoneal macrophages stimulated with CSF-1. Indeed, macrophages showed robust S6 phosphorylation after CSF-1 stimulation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Specific inhibition of PI3K p110α prevented CSF-1-induced RAE-1δ expression at low inhibitor concentrations.
source: Interestingly, specific inhibition of PI3K p110α with two different chemical inhibitors (PI3Ka2i and PI-103) prevented CSF-1-induced RAE-1δ expression at low inhibitor concentrations, whereas inhibitors of p110 isoforms β, δ, and γ only inhibited RAE-1δ induction at high inhibitor concentrations, likely due to nonspecific inhibition or off-target effects (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 6A and B.

claim: Inhibitors of p110 isoforms β, δ, and γ only inhibited RAE-1δ induction at high inhibitor concentrations, likely due to nonspecific inhibition or off-target effects.
source: Interestingly, specific inhibition of PI3K p110α with two different chemical inhibitors (PI3Ka2i and PI-103) prevented CSF-1-induced RAE-1δ expression at low inhibitor concentrations, whereas inhibitors of p110 isoforms β, δ, and γ only inhibited RAE-1δ induction at high inhibitor concentrations, likely due to nonspecific inhibition or off-target effects (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 6A and B, with speculation about the mechanism.

claim: The two PI3K p110α inhibitors also inhibited accumulation of Raet1d mRNA in CSF-1-treated macrophages.
source: The two PI3K p110α inhibitors also inhibited accumulation of Raet1d mRNA in CSF-1-treated macrophages (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by qPCR data in Figure 6C.

claim: PI3K p110α activity is required for induction of RAE-1δ gene expression by CSF-1.
source: These results indicate that PI3K p110α activity is required for induction of RAE-1δ gene expression by CSF-1.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the data presented in Figure 6.

claim: Co-culture of NK cells with CSF-1-induced macrophages expressing RAE-1 molecules efficiently downregulated NKG2D from the NK cell surface.
source: Co-culture of NK cells with CSF-1-induced macrophages expressing RAE-1 molecules efficiently downregulated NKG2D from the NK cell surface, whereas co-culture with RAE-1-KO macrophages had little to no effect on NKG2D levels (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7A.

claim: Co-culture with RAE-1-KO macrophages had little to no effect on NKG2D levels on NK cells.
source: Co-culture of NK cells with CSF-1-induced macrophages expressing RAE-1 molecules efficiently downregulated NKG2D from the NK cell surface, whereas co-culture with RAE-1-KO macrophages had little to no effect on NKG2D levels (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7A.

claim: Co-culture with RAE-1δ-expressing B16 cells led to NKG2D downregulation on NK cells.
source: Similarly, co-culture with RAE-1δ-expressing B16 cells led to NKG2D downregulation, whereas parental B16 cells had little to no effect (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7B.

claim: CSF-1-induced RAE-1δ on macrophages is capable of binding and engaging NKG2D, leading to receptor internalization.
source: Thus, CSF-1-induced RAE-1δ on macrophages is capable of binding and engaging NKG2D, leading to receptor internalization.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the data presented in Figure 7A and B.

claim: NK cells co-cultured with RAE-1δ-expressing macrophages showed an augmented functional response in vitro to anti-NKp46 stimulation compared to NK cells co-cultured with RAE-1-KO macrophages.
source: NK cells co-cultured with RAE-1δ-expressing macrophages showed an augmented functional response in vitro to anti-NKp46 stimulation compared to NK cells co-cultured with RAE-1-KO macrophages (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7C.

claim: NK cells co-cultured with B16-RAE-1δ cells showed augmented functional responses compared with NK cells co-cultured with parental B16 cells.
source: Similarly, NK cells co-cultured with B16-RAE-1δ cells showed augmented functional responses compared with NK cells co-cultured with parental B16 cells (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7D.

claim: Short-term interactions with CSF-1-stimulated macrophages expressing RAE-1δ had the effect of priming NK cells to respond better when stimulated through a distinct activating receptor in vitro.
source: These data indicate that, in this in vitro system, short-term interactions with CSF-1-stimulated macrophages expressing RAE-1δ had the effect of priming NK cells to respond better when stimulated through a distinct activating receptor.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the data presented in Figure 7C and D.

claim: The frequency of TAMs among CD45+ cells in B16 tumors was similar in WT and RAE-1-KO mice.
source: However, the frequency of TAMs among CD45+ cells in B16 tumors was similar in WT and RAE-1-KO mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: RAE-1δ levels on TAMs were similar in WT and NKG2D-KO mice.
source: To test whether NKG2D-RAE-1δ interactions select against TAMs with high RAE-1δ expression, we analyzed RAE-1δ expression on TAMs in B16 tumors in WT and NKG2D-KO mice. RAE-1δ levels on TAMs were similar in these two genotypes (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Tumor cells secrete the cytokine CSF-1, which induces the NKG2D ligand RAE-1δ on tumor-associated macrophages via a CSF-1R-PI3Kα-dependent signaling pathway.
source: Here we describe a novel cellular and molecular axis regulating NKG2D ligand expression on tumor-associated macrophages. We find that, in a set of transplant and spontaneous cancer models, tumor cells secrete the cytokine CSF-1, which induces the NKG2D ligand RAE-1δ on tumor-associated macrophages via a CSF-1R-PI3Kα-dependent signaling pathway.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion stated in the discussion based on the collective experimental data.

claim: Macrophages and monocytes were the only hematopoietic cells found to express NKG2D ligands in the tumor models studied.
source: The specificity of NKG2D ligand induction on tumor-associated hematopoietic cells was striking. Macrophages and monocytes were the only hematopoietic cells found to express NKG2D ligands, and ligand expression on those cells was completely limited to RAE-1δ.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: Ligand expression on macrophages and monocytes was completely limited to RAE-1δ.
source: The specificity of NKG2D ligand induction on tumor-associated hematopoietic cells was striking. Macrophages and monocytes were the only hematopoietic cells found to express NKG2D ligands, and ligand expression on those cells was completely limited to RAE-1δ.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: Macrophages treated with CSF-1 upregulated RAE-1δ but not other NKG2D ligands.
source: It is notable that macrophages treated with CSF-1 upregulated RAE-1δ but not other NKG2D ligands, matching the specificity of RAE-1δ induction on TAMs.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: Regulation of NKG2D ligands is tightly controlled and highly specific.
source: These data suggest that regulation of NKG2D ligands is tightly controlled and highly specific, which has also been noted in other cellular and molecular contexts.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion based on the observed specificity of RAE-1δ induction.

claim: PI3K p110α is required for macrophage RAE-1δ induction by CSF-1.
source: We show here that PI3K p110α is required for macrophage RAE-1δ by CSF-1.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: A previous study implicated PI3K p110α in NKG2D ligand induction upon in vitro MCMV infection.
source: A previous study also implicated PI3K p110α in NKG2D ligand induction upon in vitro MCMV infection (Tokuyama et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation.

claim: This report is the first to describe CSF-1 as an inducer of NKG2D ligands.
source: To our knowledge, this report is the first to describe CSF-1 as an inducer of NKG2D ligands.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a claim about the novelty of the findings.

claim: CSF-1, but not other tested cytokines, induced RAE-1δ on macrophages.
source: CSF-1, but not other tested cytokines, induced RAE-1δ on macrophages.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: Stimulation of macrophages through TLRs was found to induce RAE-1 molecules but not H60 family ligands or MULT1.
source: Stimulation of macrophages through TLRs was found to induce RAE-1 molecules but not H60 family ligands or MULT1 (Hamerman et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation.

claim: Tumor-associated myeloid cells and circulating monocytes in glioblastoma patients were found to upregulate the human NKG2D ligands ULBP1 and MICB.
source: Tumor-associated myeloid cells and circulating monocytes in glioblastoma patients were found to upregulate the human NKG2D ligands ULBP1 and MICB (Crane et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation.

claim: Dendritic cells can upregulate NKG2D ligands in vitro as a result of certain maturation conditions.
source: A handful of reports have indicated that dendritic cells can upregulate NKG2D ligands in vitro as a result of certain maturation conditions (Schrama et al., 2006; Ebihara et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations.

claim: The data presented in this manuscript represent a novel molecular signature linked to NKG2D ligand induction.
source: Thus, the data presented in this manuscript represent a novel molecular signature linked to NKG2D ligand induction.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a claim about the novelty of the findings.

claim: These data do not implicate RAE-1δ expression within the classical M1/M2 paradigm of macrophage activation.
source: Notably, these data do not implicate RAE-1δ expression within the classical (Italiani and Boraschi, 2014) -- and controversial (Martinez and Gordon, 2014) -- M1/M2 paradigm of macrophage activation.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: CSF-1 is associated with macrophage renewal and activation, but it induces a transcriptional signature distinct from M1 or M2 expression profiles.
source: CSF-1 is associated with macrophage renewal and activation, but it induces a transcriptional signature distinct from M1 or M2 expression profiles (Hume and MacDonald, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation.

claim: Classical M1 and M2 cytokines (IFNγ and IL-4, respectively) both failed to induce macrophage RAE-1δ.
source: Indeed, classical M1 and M2 cytokines (IFNγ and IL-4, respectively) both failed to induce macrophage RAE-1δ in our hands (Table 1 and not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Table 1.

claim: Induction of RAE-1δ on TAMs occurred in tumor microenvironments containing high levels of CSF-1.
source: We find here that induction RAE-1δ on TAMs occurred in tumor microenvironments containing high levels of CSF-1.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: Steady state amounts of CSF-1 are known to be present and required for maintaining monocytes and macrophages, but those concentrations were insufficient to induce RAE-1δ expression.
source: Steady state amounts of CSF-1 are known to be present and required for maintaining monocytes and macrophages, but those concentrations were insufficient to induce RAE-1δ expression.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and is based on the data showing differential CSF-1 levels and established knowledge.

claim: RAE-1δ induction requires a higher dose of CSF-1 than is necessary for survival and renewal of macrophages.
source: Hence, RAE-1δ induction requires a higher dose of CSF-1 than is necessary for survival and renewal of macrophages.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an inference from the data.

claim: Macrophage detection of elevated CSF-1 levels could be considered a sensing mechanism for local disturbances in homeostasis.
source: These considerations suggest the intriguing possibility that macrophage detection of elevated CSF-1 levels, in this case driven by dense concentrations of CSF-1-producing tumor cells, could be considered a sensing mechanism for local disturbances in homeostasis.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation based on the findings.

claim: CSF-1 is associated with macrophage programs that promote tumor growth.
source: CSF-1 is associated with macrophage programs that promote tumor growth (Hume and MacDonald, 2012), and tumor cell secretion of CSF-1 may be an adaptive feature of some cancers.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation.

claim: Tumor cell secretion of CSF-1 may be an adaptive feature of some cancers.
source: CSF-1 is associated with macrophage programs that promote tumor growth (Hume and MacDonald, 2012), and tumor cell secretion of CSF-1 may be an adaptive feature of some cancers.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation.

claim: Macrophage RAE-1δ had a stimulatory effect in an in vitro co-culture model, as short-term incubation of CSF-1-stimulated RAE-1δ-expressing macrophages with NK cells caused elevated NK responses to subsequent acute stimulation compared to incubation with macrophages lacking RAE-1 molecules.
source: Indeed, in the current study, macrophage RAE-1δ had a stimulatory effect in an in vitro co-culture model, as short-term incubation of CSF-1-stimulated RAE-1δ-expressing macrophages with NK cells caused elevated NK responses to subsequent acute stimulation compared to incubation with macrophages lacking RAE-1 molecules.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: Expression of RAE-1 molecules on mononuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cells in certain tumor-bearing mice has a stimulatory effect on NK cells in a co-culture setting.
source: These findings are similar to a previous study showing that expression of RAE-1 molecules on mononuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cells in certain tumor-bearing mice has a stimulatory effect on NK cells in a co-culture setting (Nausch et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation.

claim: A recent study employed antibody blockade and genetic deletion studies to show that endogenously expressed RAE-1ε ligated NKG2D and desensitized NK cells in steady state conditions and in tumors, whereas RAE-1δ had little or no effect on NKG2D levels or desensitization.
source: However, a recent study from our laboratory employed antibody blockade and genetic deletion studies to show that endogenously expressed RAE-1ε ligated NKG2D and desensitized NK cells in steady state conditions and in tumors, whereas RAE-1δ had little or no effect on NKG2D levels or desensitization (Thompson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation.

claim: The impact of RAE-1 expressed by hematopoietic cells was relatively modest.
source: Furthermore, bone marrow chimera experiments in that study demonstrated that the impact of RAE-1 expressed by hematopoietic cells was relatively modest (Thompson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation.

claim: WT and RAE-1-KO mice had similar macrophage numbers in B16 tumors.
source: However, WT and RAE-1-KO mice had similar macrophage numbers in B16 tumors, and TAM RAE-1δ levels were similar in WT and NKG2D-KO mice.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: The frequency or duration of the interaction between NKG2D and RAE-1δ may modulate its functional effect on NK cells, revealing different effects in vitro vs. in vivo.
source: It is possible that the frequency or duration of the interaction between NKG2D and RAE-1δ may modulate its functional effect on NK cells, revealing different effects in vitro vs. in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation about the findings.

claim: Other signals in the tumor environment may influence the outcome of NKG2D-RAE-1δ interactions.
source: Or, perhaps other signals in the tumor environment influence this outcome.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation.

source: It is also possible that RAE-1δ on TAMs has an as-yet-undiscovered effect on macrophage biology or other features of the tumor microenvironment.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation.

claim: A previous report documented expression of RAE-1 molecules in microglia in mice with experimental allergic encephalitis, and RAE-1 mRNA expression was found to correlate with CSF-1-induced microglial proliferation in vitro.
source: Indeed, a previous report documented expression of RAE-1 molecules in microglia in mice with experimental allergic encephalitis, and RAE-1 mRNA expression was found to correlate with CSF-1-induced microglial proliferation in vitro (Djelloul et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation.

claim: Macrophage RAE-1δ may interact with and modulate other NKG2D-expressing cells in tumors.
source: It is also possible that macrophage RAE-1δ interacts with and modulates other NKG2D-expressing cells in tumors.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation.

claim: Tumor-associated macrophages are identified as CD45-pos; CD11b-hi; Ly6G-neg; F4/80-hi.
source: Tumor-associated macrophages (hereafter called TAMs) are an important subset of myeloid cells identified as CD45-pos; CD11b-hi; Ly6G-neg; F4/80-hi (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by the gating strategy shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Monocytes in B16 tumors are identified as CD45-pos; CD11b-hi; Ly6G-neg; F4/80-low; Ly6C-hi.
source: In addition to strong expression on TAMs, RAE-1δ was weakly expressed on monocytes in B16 tumors (identified as CD45-pos; CD11b-hi; Ly6G-neg; F4/80-low; Ly6C-hi – gating strategy in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A) – but negligible on other hematopoietic cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by the gating strategy shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A.
